candidates.title: onCancel Type Issue: Missing Keyboard Event Support
candidates.origin: repo:ant-design/ant-design is:issue is:closed keyboard in:title (batch-twenty-one query cap)
candidates.issueBody:
### Reproduction link

[https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4.24.16/components/modal/Modal.tsx#L59](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4.24.16/components/modal/Modal.tsx#L59)

### Steps to reproduce

https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4.24.16/components/modal/Modal.tsx#L59

### What is expected?

The issue is that when a user presses Esc, it triggers a KeyboardEvent, not a MouseEvent. The current typing would cause TypeScript errors if you try to handle keyboard events in the callback.

If this is for an Ant Design Modal component, you might want to check their official types, as they typically use a union type or a more generic event type to handle both mouse clicks and keyboard events

### What is actually happening?

Looking at that TypeScript definition, there's a potential issue with the type. The onCancel callback is typed to only accept React.MouseEvent<HTMLElement>, but based on the comment, it should also handle keyboard events (Esc key).

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | undefined |
| React | 16 |
| System | windows |
| Browser | chrome |

---
The current type:

onCancel?: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLElement>) => void;
Should probably be:

onCancel?: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLElement> | React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => void;
Or more generically:

onCancel?: (e: React.SyntheticEvent<HTMLElement>) => void;

comments.body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @codechallengesJS! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the ant-design team.

<!-- Answer -->
You're right—currently, the Modal component's onCancel prop is typed to accept only React.MouseEvent, so handling keyboard events like Esc will cause TypeScript errors, even though the Modal logic does support closing via keyboard interaction (Esc key) internally. This typing limitation is present in both older and the latest versions of Ant Design ModalProps ([source](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/3810d1dc6a24cbfe08805a28d54abb2332fbbbec/components/modal/interface.ts#L71-L189)).

Recent PRs and tests confirm that keyboard events are handled in Modal's behavior ([example](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/56386)), but the onCancel type definition hasn't been updated to reflect this. There are ongoing discussions and plans to unify and improve event typing for close/cancel props in Ant Design 6.x ([discussion](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/54394)), but as of now, the type is still MouseEvent only.

If you need to handle both mouse and keyboard events in onCancel, you can use a type assertion or cast the event to any as a workaround. Alternatively, you can define your handler to accept React.SyntheticEvent or a union of MouseEvent and KeyboardEvent, but you'll need to override the type locally until the official types are updated.

You can track progress or join the discussion here: [Modal close/cancel typing unification](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/54394).

candidates.issueBody:
### Reproduction link

[https://ant.design/components/select/](https://ant.design/components/select/)

### Steps to reproduce

1. navigate via the keyboard to a select dropdown
2. press spacebar to open the dropdown

### What is expected?

The spacebar press will open the select dropdown

### What is actually happening?

The page scrolls

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | 6.2.3 |
| React | latest |
| System | latest |
| Browser | latest |

---
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/combobox_role#enter_2

comments.body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @abel-eero! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the ant-design team.

<!-- Answer -->
This is a known accessibility issue: the Select component delegates keyboard handling to rc-select, and currently, pressing the spacebar does not open the dropdown as required by ARIA combobox standards (which specify that spacebar should toggle the popup) [MDN ARIA combobox](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/combobox_role#enter_2). The Ant Design codebase does not implement explicit spacebar handling for Select; all keyboard logic is in rc-select, which is not included in this repo and has similar open issues for other components as well [source](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/31284).

As a workaround, you can intercept the spacebar key with an `onKeyDown` handler on the Select trigger element to manually open the dropdown, similar to solutions suggested for Tabs and Dropdown accessibility issues [source](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/53612). For now, if you need strict ARIA compliance, you may need to implement this workaround until rc-select or Ant Design addresses the issue upstream. Keep an eye on rc-select and Ant Design changelogs for future accessibility improvements.

candidates.title: Borderless inputs: no focus styles
candidates.origin: repo:ant-design/ant-design is:issue is:closed focus in:title (batch-twenty-one query cap)
candidates.issueBody:
### Reproduction link

[https://ant.design/components/input#input-demo-variant](https://ant.design/components/input#input-demo-variant)

### Steps to reproduce

Use Tab navigation to focus borderless (`variant="borderless"`) element:
- `Input` (https://ant.design/components/input#input-demo-variant)
- `InputNumber` (https://ant.design/components/input-number#input-number-demo-variant)
- `Select` (https://ant.design/components/select#select-demo-variant)
- `DatePicker` (https://ant.design/components/date-picker#date-picker-demo-variant)
- `TimePicker` (https://ant.design/components/time-picker#time-picker-demo-variant)
- `AutoComplete` (https://ant.design/components/auto-complete#auto-complete-demo-variant)
- `Cascader` (https://ant.design/components/cascader#cascader-demo-variant)
- `Mentions` (https://ant.design/components/mentions#mentions-demo-variant)
- `TreeSelect` (https://ant.design/components/tree-select#tree-select-demo-variant)

### What is expected?

The element to have focus styles, either border or box shadow or something else.

### What is actually happening?

Transparent color is used for focused state https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/master/components/select/style/select-input.ts#L410 (`Select` example), that's why the element has no focus styles. It breaks WCAG success criterion 2.4.7 (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html).

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | 6.4.3 |
| React | 19 |
| System | Windows 11 |
| Browser | Google Chrome latest |

<!-- generated by ant-design-issue-helper. DO NOT REMOVE -->

comments.body:
<!-- Answer -->
This is a valid accessibility concern. You're correct that the borderless variant explicitly uses transparent colors for focus-related properties across multiple components.

**Root cause:** The Select's borderless variant sets `borderActive: 'transparent'` and `borderOutline: 'transparent'` in the focused state [[1]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4a0fb237728e0a96841ad447a3d8d2a1f8badd77/components/select/style/select-input.ts#L405-L413). Similarly, the shared `genBorderlessStyle` function in `components/input/style/variants.ts` applies `outline: 'none'` without providing an alternative focus indicator [[2]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4a0fb237728e0a96841ad447a3d8d2a1f8badd77/components/input/style/variants.ts#L194-L196). This pattern affects InputNumber, DatePicker, Mentions, and other components that share this styling approach [[3]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4a0fb237728e0a96841ad447a3d8d2a1f8badd77/components/input-number/style/index.ts#L6-L10) [[4]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4a0fb237728e0a96841ad447a3d8d2a1f8badd77/components/date-picker/style/variants.ts#L4-L9) [[5]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/4a0fb237728e0a96841ad447a3d8d2a1f8badd77/components/mentions/style/index.ts#L12-L17).

**Existing infrastructure:** The codebase already has centralized `genFocusOutline(token)` and `genFocusStyle(token)` utilities that provide proper `:focus-visible` styling using design tokens [[6]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/57266). These have been applied to fix focus accessibility in other areas — Input clear buttons [[7]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/57432), DatePicker/TimePicker clear buttons [[8]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/58132), Alert close buttons [[9]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/57695), and Tree/TreeSelect nodes [[10]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/56716).

However, the borderless variant's container focus styling hasn't been addressed yet. The fix would involve replacing the transparent focus colors with proper `:focus-visible` styles (e.g., a subtle box-shadow or outline) using the existing `genFocusOutline`/`genFocusStyle` utilities, applied consistently across all affected components (Input, InputNumber, Select, DatePicker, TimePicker, AutoComplete, Cascader, Mentions, TreeSelect).

### Steps to reproduce

comments.body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @ownlight6! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the ant-design team.

<!-- Answer -->
这是一个已知的 token 派生逻辑导致的问题。当 `colorPrimary` 设置为深色（如 `'#333'`）时，`controlOutline` 是通过 `colorPrimary` → 色板生成 → `colorPrimaryBg`（最浅色） → `getAlphaColor()` alpha 混合 三个阶段派生出来的 [[1]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/ac5e68423b6fb7d98704ea8028bd10e290847048/components/theme/util/alias.ts#L99)。由于原始颜色本身就很深，生成的 `colorPrimaryBg` 也偏暗 [[2]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/ac5e68423b6fb7d98704ea8028bd10e290847048/components/theme/themes/shared/genColorMapToken.ts#L54)，最终 `controlOutline` 就会产生过深的 box-shadow。

**临时解决方案**：你可以通过 token 覆盖来单独控制 focus 的 shadow：

```tsx
<ConfigProvider
  theme={{
    token: {
      colorPrimary: '#333',
      controlOutline: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)', // 手动设置更浅的 outline
    },
  }}
>
```

或者使用组件级别的 token 只针对 Input 组件调整 [[3]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/56261)：

```tsx
<ConfigProvider
  theme={{
    token: { colorPrimary: '#333' },
    components: {
      Input: {
        activeShadow: '0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)',
      },
    },
  }}
>
```

从设计系统角度来看，`controlOutline` 的派生算法在 `colorPrimary` 为极深色时确实不够理想，类似的暗色场景适配问题在 PR #57511 [[4]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/57511) 中已经对 shadow token 做了改进，但 `controlOutline` 的计算逻辑尚未做类似的自适应处理。


<!-- Dosu Comment Footer -->

candidates.issueBody:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I am using the [correct version](https://github.com/react-bootstrap/react-bootstrap#bootstrap-compatibility) of React-Bootstrap for my version of Bootstrap
- [X] I have [searched](https://github.com/react-bootstrap/react-bootstrap/issues?q=is%3Aissue) for duplicate or closed issues
- [X] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/react-bootstrap/react-bootstrap/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Describe the bug

Focus and tabbing can leave the modal despite `enforceFocus={true}`.

### Expected behavior

Focus and tabbing should be limited to the modal.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a modal with a bunch of interactive elements in it.
2. Open a modal.
3. Keep tabbing until the focus is on the last element.
4. The next tab will make the focus leave the modal altogether instead of wrapping.

### Reproducible Example

Any example from the [documentation](https://react-bootstrap.github.io/components/modal/), e.g. [live demo](https://react-bootstrap.github.io/components/modal/#modal-props). 

### Screenshots

_No response_

### What operating system(s) are you seeing the problem on?

Linux

### What browser(s) are you seeing the problem on?

Firefox

### What version of React-Bootstrap are you using?

2.7.2

### What version of Bootstrap are you using?

5.3.0-alpha3

### Additional context

Unreproducible with vanilla Bootstrap. There the tabbing order works as expected and is contained within the modal.

comments.body: Focus should wrap, keep hitting tab (unless you have it turned off with enforceFocus=false). Focus moves to the end of the modal then out of the window to the url bar and then back to the modal, this is how native dialogs work as well and an area that RB does better than most JS modals that trap focus in the window

But that's not how it works in [vanilla Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/components/modal/#live-demo), is it? WAI-ARIA also recommends containment of focus/tabbing:
> The [aria-modal](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-modal) [attribute](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-attribute) is used to indicate that the presence of a "modal" element precludes usage of other content on the page. For example, when a modal dialog is displayed, it is expected that the user's interaction is limited to the contents of the dialog, until the modal dialog loses focus or is no longer displayed.

In my specific scenario, the next tab moves the focus onto the last element (a link in the footer), and consequently, scrolls the backdrop all the way down. That's not a good experience in my opinion. Ideally, both focus and tabbing are contained within a dialog as described in the [guidelines](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).

I want to make one thing clear: `react-bootstrap` is absolutely awesome and I wouldn't trade it for anything. However, that doesn't mean it's perfect and free of bugs or quirks. Sorry if that came across as mean. My intentions were never to compare it to other frameworks or even put it down.

Sorry, i'm not being defensive or upset just explaining that this is intentional and thought out. It differs from vanilla bootstrap because we believe that it's better to be closer to the correct behavior than to match upstream. 

What the guidelines mean when they say "focus should be contained" is that a dialog should act as the entire document for the page, e.g. behave as if it was the only element rendered in the page. Normal document tab flow allows the focus to move out of the document to the browser UI when you reach the end, and then cycle back to the first element from the browser UI when you keep tabbing. This is the behavior we are trying to emulate and something that other JS modals fail to do correctly.

Notice that this is how the native `dialog` element works https://5qyc7e.csb.app/ as well which is the gold standard for correct accessibility. The one tradeoff tho we had to make to get this to work correctly is the scrolling issue sometimes happens which we would love to fix (and maybe we can) but overall we believe it's better to have the more correct a11y behavior if we need to pick.

The spec makes it clear that user interaction should not leak outside a modal. You could argue that the user should still be able to tab to the browser's UI (which is how the `dialog` element behaves) but leaving the rest of the page sequentially focusable doesn't make any sense. As I described before, it leads to page scrolls and a "jumpy" behavior.

[APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/) is also unambiguous in this regard even if it's less authoritative to a degree.

At the moment, `Modal` is not quite on par with the `dialog` element. While it's open, the elements outside of it are tabable, which scrolls the main document.

Happy to accept PRs to address the case where focus jumps, just not at the expense of trapping focus inside the window permanently! From an a11y perspective we are happy with it's behavior and have verified it works well with experts.

I have recently upgraded react-modal from 1.7.1 to 3.1.6. I am now getting a warning in the console whenever react-modal unmounts. 

### Steps to reproduce:
 1. Mount a component that is using React Modal as a child.
 2. Dismount the component has has React Modal as a child.  (this happens for me when I navigate between routes)

### Expected behavior:
 1. I'm not sure if this warning is due to incorrect implementation on my part or if this is expected behavior. 

### Additional notes:
The modals are behaving normally, I am just unsure why the focus manager is giving me this warning.

comments.body: Hi @Jacob-Allen, before the modal is open, it will put in a queue the `document.activeElement`, so it can try to return the focus after the modal is closed. So, if this element doesn't exist in the next route this warn will be presented.

Hey @diasbruno, 
It is often that the modal is never opened on certain pages. Is there anything I can do to drop it from the queue before I dismount the component so that I can circumvent this warning?
There is an option we added recently - `shouldReturnFocusAfterClose={bool}`. If false, it will be no-op when pop out of the queue.
It should work fine in case where you can jump to other pages from the modal, but if it's not the case, it may cause some accessibility issues.
I'll keep this open, because this feature is not documented.

@diasbruno, I am also getting this warning more than a dozen times. It does not happen when I run my app in the browser, but when I run my tests. I see that the logic for displaying this warning has existed for some time now, but I only started seeing it when I upgrade to v3.1.7.

I don't fully understand why this warning is being shown to me. It occurs on components that have modals in them, but they are closed by default, so I'm curious why would they ever be attempting to "return focus" when they shouldn't have been muddling with the focus in the first place (since they are all closed).

> before the modal is open, it will put in a queue the document.activeElement, so it can try to return the focus after the modal is closed.

Doh, I missed this my first read through! So the modals are adding to the queue _before_ they are open, i.e. when they are rendered.

I can remove the error by not manually unmounting my component (removing `ReactDOM.unmountComponentAtNode(node)` from my smoke test), which come to think of it seems fine.

I suppose I hadn't considered this when I first started writing my tests, but there is usually no reason to manually unmount (only caveat is when testing things like `<ReactModal>` open/close directly, since exiting a test with a modal open will pollute `document.body.classList`, which could affect other tests). I think it would be safe to remove the manual unmount call for my smoke tests, which also resolves my issue of seeing this warning so many times when running tests.

Thanks!

Hi @royrwood ,

@diasbruno mentioned that there is an undocumented prop to bypass the focusmanager. By adding `shouldReturnFocusAfterClose={false}` to the Modal it will opt out of the focus handler. I have the parent component set this value to false in the componentWillUnmount and it has caused the warning to go away.
This is actually documented on the [https://reactcommunity.org/react-modal/](https://reactcommunity.org/react-modal/). (sorry)

The problem with this is that I don't want to opt out of the focus manager. I just want to be able to render components in my test without every component that has a modal attached to it throwing this warning.

This check in `returnFocus` as it stands now is making a huge assumption in that it **never** expects a component to be manually unmounted, which is unrealistic.

This will warn on any test that unmounts—including Enzyme unmounts—and will even show the warning with the [default CRA setup](https://github.com/facebookincubator/create-react-app/pull/3511).

@indiesquidge 
I definitely agree that this should not be the default behavior. I agree that this opt out should not be required. 

I opened this issue because I think the part of 
> making a huge assumption

is in fact an undesirable feature in the current implementation of this package.

I have only referenced this workaround as a way to silence the warning, not as justification of a permanent intended fix.

I know the warning could simply be removed, but ideally the contributors will expand on this logic and auto opt out of the focus manager before a dismount.

> It is often that the modal is never opened on certain pages.

@Jacob-Allen  I miss this part. :)

@Jacob-Allen @indiesquidge @royrwood 

Here is a place to dig in [Modal.js#L144](https://github.com/reactjs/react-modal/blob/master/src/components/Modal.js#L144). It's possible that on `componentWillUnmount` of the modal is scheduling the close action event when already closed.

@diasbruno, I think I may need a bit more context to understand the scope of this issue if I am to help find an adequate solution.

> Using the mounted flag on `afterClose` looks a bit weird because the only way it can/should be called is if the `ModalPortal` is actually mounted.

Could you explain why you think `afterClose` is being called when it shouldn't be? From what I understand (and from what other people are reporting here), `ModalPortal` is mounted when _the component using the modal is mounted_, not when the modal itself is opened. (This can be verified in the examples by putting console statements in `componentWillUnmount` and observing that the function is never called save on the React Router example.)

One could say that `afterClose` is perhaps poorly named (or at the very least does not make sense to be invoked in `componentWillUnmount` with all of its current behavior), but I don't see why it shouldn't be called.

> Here is a place to dig in Modal.js#L144. It's possible that on componentWillUnmount of the modal is scheduling the close action event when already closed.

@diasbruno, I think I am confused by your recommendation here. `<Modal>` does not seem to make any reference to the `focusManager`—don't we want to be looking for a fix in `<ModalPortal>`, or am I misunderstanding something?
I'm referring to a possible path that can trigger `afterClose`.
@indiesquidge looks good!

candidates.issueBody: # Bug report We're using a controlled Popover with openOnHover={true} and expect the Popover content to also open when the trigger receives keyboard focus. When the user navigates to the trigger using the keyboard (for example, by pressing Tab), the Popover should open and display its main content in the same way it does when the trigger is hovered. However, the current behavior conflicts with Base UI's internal focus management and can result in the Popover reopening unexpectedly after dismissal. ## Current behavior 1.With openOnHover={true}, hovering over the trigger opens the Popover as expected. 2.When the trigger receives keyboard focus through Tab navigation, the Popover does not reliably open/display its main content as expected. 3.Attempting to manually open the controlled Popover from the trigger's onFocus can cause the Popover to immediately reopen when focus returns to the trigger after dismissal. 4.Clicking outside does not reliably dismiss the Popover in this scenario. 5.In some cases, FloatingFocusManager throws the following error: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded ## Expected behavior When openOnHover={true}, the Popover should also open when the trigger receives keyboard focus. For example: 1.User tabs to the Popover trigger. 2.The trigger receives focus. 3.The Popover opens and displays its main content. 4.The user can continue keyboard navigation into the Popover content. 5.The user can dismiss the Popover normally. 6.After dismissal, the Popover should remain closed until the trigger is intentionally hovered or focused again. Opening the Popover on keyboard focus should not cause it to immediately reopen after dismissal or when focus returns to the trigger. ## Reproducible example ```tsx const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); Help } /> Focusable link The issue can also be reproduced by explicitly opening the controlled Popover from the trigger's onFocus: const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); setOpen(true)}> Help } /> Focusable link ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1.Set openOnHover={true} on the Popover. 2.Navigate to the trigger using the keyboard (Tab). 3.Observe that the Popover should open and display its main content. 4.Move focus into the Popover content. 5.Continue tabbing or click outside to dismiss the Popover. 6.Observe the Popover's dismissal/reopening behavior. 7.In some cases, FloatingFocusManager throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. ## Base UI version v1.7.0 ## Which browser are you using? Chrome ## Which OS are you using? Mac OS ## Which assistive tech are you using (if applicable)? Not Applicable ## Additional context Our requirement is that a Popover configured with openOnHover={true} should also expose its content when the trigger receives keyboard focus, so that keyboard users have equivalent access to the Popover content. Is supporting open on keyboard focus together with openOnHover a supported interaction pattern in Base UI? If so, is there a recommended implementation that works with Base UI's internal focus management and dismissal behavior? In particular, we would like to avoid manually calling setOpen(true) from the trigger's onFocus if that conflicts with Base UI's focus management.

comments.body:
> **Our requirement** is that a Popover configured with openOnHover={true} should also expose its content when the trigger receives keyboard focus, so that keyboard users have equivalent access to the Popover content.

Hey @rachabharadwaj0707-eng, can you explain why this is a requirement? 

> Is supporting open on keyboard focus together with openOnHover a supported interaction pattern in Base UI?

Opening on focus isn't a supported pattern for Popover intentionally.

`openOnHover` is merely a pointer convenience on top of the standard click-to-open behavior for keyboard access. Keyboard users tab to the trigger and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> to open it. Opening on focus alone would force an interactive popup on users who are just tabbing past the trigger (with interactive content, this borders on a WCAG 3.2.1 (On Focus) context-change violation). So in other words, `hover` for pointer users is not safely equivalent to `focus` for keyboard users.

The loop you're encountering is an indication of why this pattern is usually avoided.
Opening on focus only works for popups that never take focus, which is why Tooltip and PreviewCard support it but Popover doesn't. There's usually little to no reliable way to distinguish "user tabbed to the trigger" from "focus was restored to the trigger" as the interaction is intrinsically loopy.
Since the issue is missing key information and has been inactive for 7 days, it has been automatically closed. If you wish to see the issue reopened, please provide the missing information.

candidates.title: [radio] An arrow key the group ignores still arms "select the next radio to take focus"
candidates.origin: repo:mui/base-ui is:issue is:closed focus in:title (batch-twenty-one query cap)
candidates.reason: Fix5643 identified; no stable working baseline established. Existing supported plain ArrowDown single-enabled variant can be considered only after source qualification.
candidates.issueBody:
### Summary

`RadioGroup` arms "select the next radio that takes focus" on **any** `Arrow*` keydown, and only `Radio.Root`'s `onFocus` disarms it. When the arrow moves no focus, the flag stays armed after the user leaves the group. The next radio to take focus is then selected - a value the user never picked.

Two ways to press an arrow that moves nothing:

- **A modifier is held.** `RadioGroup` passes `modifierKeys: [SHIFT]`, so `useCompositeRoot` returns early for `Meta`/`Control`/`Alt` and no focus moves. `Meta+ArrowDown` is a normal "scroll to the bottom" key.
- **Fewer than two enabled radios.** `nextIndex === highlightedIndex`, so no focus event fires.

Blur does not help: `RadioGroup`'s `onBlur` calls `setFieldTouched`, not `setTouched`.

Relevant code in 1.7.0:

- `radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx` - `onKeyDownCapture` runs `setTouched(true)` for every `event.key.startsWith('Arrow')`
- `radio/root/RadioRoot.tsx` - `onFocus` calls `inputRef.current?.click()` when `touched`, then `setTouched(false)`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Render a `RadioGroup` with nothing selected.
2. Focus a radio and press `Meta+ArrowDown`. Nothing moves, which is correct.
3. Tab out of the group, then Tab back in.
4. The radio that takes focus is now selected.

Same with step 2 replaced by a plain `ArrowDown` in a group where only one radio is enabled.

### Current vs expected behavior

The group selects a value the user never chose. An arrow key that moves no focus should not arm the selection.

### Reproduction

`@base-ui/react` 1.7.0, React 19, vitest + jsdom + React Testing Library. The first two cases are controls; the last two fail the way the title says.

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import '@testing-library/jest-dom'
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { RadioGroup } from '@base-ui/react/radio-group'
import { Radio } from '@base-ui/react/radio'

const TwoEnabled = () => (
  <RadioGroup defaultValue="">
    <Radio.Root value="yes" nativeButton render={<button type="button" />}>Yes</Radio.Root>
    <Radio.Root value="no" nativeButton render={<button type="button" />}>No</Radio.Root>
  </RadioGroup>
)

const OneEnabled = () => (
  <RadioGroup defaultValue="">
    <Radio.Root value="yes" nativeButton render={<button type="button" />}>Yes</Radio.Root>
    <Radio.Root value="no" nativeButton render={<button type="button" />} disabled>No</Radio.Root>
  </RadioGroup>
)

const radio = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('radio', { name })
const leaveAndComeBack = () => {
  radio('Yes').blur()
  radio('Yes').focus()
}

describe('@base-ui/react 1.7.0 RadioGroup', () => {
  it('CONTROL: refocus alone does not select', () => {
    render(<TwoEnabled />)
    radio('Yes').focus()
    leaveAndComeBack()
    expect(radio('Yes')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'false')
  })

  it('CONTROL: a plain arrow moves the selection (intended)', async () => {
    render(<TwoEnabled />)
    radio('Yes').focus()
    fireEvent.keyDown(radio('Yes'), { key: 'ArrowDown' })
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(radio('No')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true'))
  })

  it('BUG: Meta+Arrow moves nothing, but arms the next focus', () => {
    render(<TwoEnabled />)
    radio('Yes').focus()
    fireEvent.keyDown(radio('Yes'), { key: 'ArrowDown', metaKey: true })
    expect(radio('Yes')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'false')
    leaveAndComeBack()
    expect(radio('Yes')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true') // should still be false
  })

  it('BUG: an arrow with nowhere to go arms the next focus', () => {
    render(<OneEnabled />)
    radio('Yes').focus()
    fireEvent.keyDown(radio('Yes'), { key: 'ArrowDown' })
    expect(radio('Yes')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'false')
    leaveAndComeBack()
    expect(radio('Yes')).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true') // should still be false
  })
})
```

### Workaround

An `onKeyDownCapture` on the group that calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` for an arrow the group cannot act on.

### Context

We hit this in a patient medical form, where the group ends up showing an answer the patient never gave.

candidates.origin: repo:mui/base-ui is:issue is:closed focus in:title (batch-twenty-one query cap)

candidates.issueBody:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

If you tab into the number field for the first time after page load, the caret gets placed at the end of the value with nothing selected, so typing appends to the existing number (you get `1005` instead of replacing and having just `5`). But if you tab out and back in, the whole value is selected and typing replaces it.

So the same action (tabbing into the field) behaves differently depending on whether it's the first focus or not.

Easy to repro in the docs https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field:

1. fresh page load
2. tab until you reach the Amount input -> caret at the end, no selection
3. tab away, then shift+tab back -> whole value selected

Looks like it's caused by `NumberFieldInput.tsx` in `onFocus` that moves the caret to the end on the first focus only, guarded by `hasTouchedInputRef`:

```js
if (hasTouchedInputRef.current) {
  return;
}
hasTouchedInputRef.current = true;

// Browsers set selection at the start of the input field by default. We want to set it at
// the end for the first focus.
const target = event.currentTarget;
const length = target.value.length;
target.setSelectionRange(length, length);
```

The comment about browsers putting the caret at the start is true for programmatic `.focus()` (like when clicking the increment/decrement buttons), but for keyboard tab the browser default is selecting the whole value. Since the handler doesn't check how the focus happened, the override also eats the first tab-in.

## Expected behavior

Tabbing into the field should behave the same every time so it probably should select everything, including the first time.

## Reproducible example

https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field (the hero demo at the top)

## Base UI version

v1.7.0

## Which browser are you using?

Chrome

## Which OS are you using?

Windows 11

## Which assistive tech are you using (if applicable)?

n/a

## Additional context

Provide any additional context that might help us identify the problem and find a solution.
